backend/docs/changes.md.reason: A DOC-ONLY row. It records that no suite re-run happened and quotes a scoped retention-class run plus the figures the earlier cycle measured, so a floor artifact for this task would record the whole suite on some other commit rather than what the row says. Backfilling one would attach a measurement to a sentence that never made it.

A lint and format row, and its own counted figures (the lint errors, the distinct rules, the files the formatter rewrote) are ruff's output rather than a suite floor. The floor it also quotes was measured on that commit, before the printer existed. `floor --task GATE-1` run now measures the current tree, so the artifact it would write records a different tree than the row describes -- an artifact that satisfies the gate's existence test while vouching for something else.

A PostgreSQL row written before the printer existed and edited by a later cycle in this train, so the diff against a promotion base reports the whole row as added even though the figures in it are two cycles old. `floor --task GATE-3` measures the current tree on both engines and would record a different figure from the one the row prints, so the artifact cannot be backfilled honestly. Its `failures=N` figures are the pg gate's certified failure count on that commit, not a mutation replay, and scripts/mutation_evidence.py holds no manifest for this task because no mutation was ever recorded against it.

The row that turned branch coverage on, and it quotes the same suite measured twice on that commit -- once line-only, once branch-inclusive -- to show the setting is doing work. `floor` records one run per engine and cannot record a line-only and a branch-inclusive reading of the same commit, and running it now measures the tree as it stands rather than as it stood when the decision was taken.

The discovery-guard row. `Ran 0 tests / NO TESTS RAN` is the COUNTER-EXAMPLE the row carries in order to show the guard catches a suite that cannot be found; it is the output of a deliberately broken discovery, not a floor. No artifact can record it, and writing one that 'backs' it would be fabricating a measurement of a failure nobody ran. The row's remaining figures are the collected/declared counts of the step replayed in git bash, which `floor` does not record either.

The nightly claim-scan row. Its headline figure is the scanner's own error count over the whole corpus and the exit code it decided the job on, read from `scripts/doc_claims.py --base`; `floor` records a suite run and a coverage TOTAL row and has no field for either, so there is nothing here for an artifact to match.
